critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct and defense-in-depth: (1) ['first party']/['second party'] loose rules are re-enabled on *_name only, enabling match on plain 'First Party' / 'Second Party' labels on the real SHCIL form; (2) neg:['mobile','phone','email','e-mail','address','pin','pan','proof','identity','residence'] on *_name and neg:['mobile','phone','email','e-mail','pin','pan'] on *_address, together with scoreField short-circuiting to 0 when any neg token appears in context, guarantees a *_name field can never match an address/mobile/email/pin/pan labelled field; (3) new first/second_party_address1/2/3 rules with explicit 'address line N' tokens correctly map address boxes.

setVal SELECT uses bidirectional substring matching (both ways); still a latent risk if option labels overlap (e.g., 'First Party' matches both 'First Party' and 'First Party (Buyer)') but not a current blocker since the mock options are disjoint.
FIELDS mapping is now the source of truth and remains compact; consider in future adding a unit test (e.g., jest/vitest) that imports FIELDS directly instead of extracting via regex from the source.

rca of the issue: Prior bug: strict rules [['first party','name']] didn't match the real SHCIL label which is simply 'First Party' (no 'name' token), so #ctl00_cph_txtFp stayed blank. FIX in /app/frontend/src/lib/bookmarklet.js: added loose fallback rule ['first party'] / ['second party'] to first/second_party_name, guarded by neg:['mobile','phone','email','e-mail','address','pin','pan','proof','identity','residence'] so the loose match cannot land in an address/mobile/email box. Added explicit first/second_party_address1/2/3 fields with rules ['<party>','address line N']/['<party>','address N'] + names hints (fpadd1, spadd1). scoreField() returns 0 whenever a neg token is found in field context, providing belt-and-suspenders defense. Verified live on mock: party-name boxes now populate; empty address/email stays blank; no cross-contamination.
